Waterphone Strings:
Waterphone Strings:  Waterphone response convolution is applied to a string emulating preset. An oscillator whose spectral balance is controlled with X, Y and Z in a sawtooth-like range to get a dynamic string timbre is sent into a low pass filter and to the outputs as well as into a tapped delay. A second oscillator with sine LFO modulation applied to its frequency and very high spectral balance (again controlled with X, Y and Z)is sent to outputs and also into the delay. This second component adds a more buzzing/raspy string sound component as well as a slight background vibrato. Finally bandpass filtered noise is output (but not sent into the delay) to simulate bowed string slipping/noise.

Note: The delay is sent out all four taps to differing stereo channels as well as the main delay Bank C. Each tap has sine LFO modulation applied to the delay at slighly different speed ratios and each tap's LFO Macro is 90 degrees out of phase with the next. This all serves to create a more bowed, organically complex yet fluid result.

Macro i (Waterphone): This controls the current convolution interpolation point between the Waterphone1 and Waterphone 2 responses. It also increases sustain on the delay outputs through control of blended Persistence.
Macro ii (ChLevel): Controls the level of the delayed/tapped outputs.
Macro iii (ChSpeed): Controls the speed of the LFO modulation applied to the delay and taps.
Macro iv (ChDepth): Controls the depth (delay percentage) of the max delay time that will be applied. Because the max delay is set to 50ms, this is a subtle effect (many of the EaganMatrix string emulations use fine and subtle changes to create a more natural sound).
v (Release): Sustain afer release through a blend of Persistence applied to all the SL/SR output formulas.

WaveBank - Basic:
Basic WaveBank: A WaveBank is a bank of one to five frequency assignable waves that can be selected as Sawtooth, Square or Triangle. A duty cycle and weighting are also available as parameters. It is common to assign X as the base frequency and then assign one or more octaves to get a big multi-octave sound mass (as is done in this preset). The WaveBank lets you experiment with simple additive synthesis and is useful for creating organ sounds of all types.

Note: When you use a WaveBank, it occupies half the memory of the VoiceDelay, SummedDelay, MicroDelay, and FormulaDelay. If you have one WaveBank (in Bank A or Bank B), you can also have a VoiceDelay, SummedDelay, MicroDelay, and FormulaDelay in Bank C (which will operate using half its normal memory). If you have two WaveBanks (both Bank A and Bank B) as well as a Delay in Bank C, both WaveBanks must specify the same kind of wave (Sawtooth, Square, or Triangle wave).

Macro i (Duty): Duty cycle for waves generated by the WaveBank. Values range from 0 to 1 (or equivalently, 0 to -1). Value 0 is normal; if the WaveBank has Square selected, 0 is a 50% duty cycle square, and nonzero is a pulse wave.
Macro ii (Weighting): Weighting of the amplitudes of the waves generated by the WaveBank. 0 is equal weighting. Values higher than 0 up to 1 favor even numbered waves, and values lower than 0 to -1 favor odd numbered waves.
Note: This parameter can also be changed to Duty Offset: Offset for the D column's Duty Cycle value. The offset is added once to the second wave in the WaveBank, twice to the third, etc. YOu will have to do that in the matrix.

Macro iii (LFOMod): Sine based LFO modulation width on the Duty Cycle that will be applied if set > 0. 
Macro iv (LFOSpeed): Frequency of the LFO modulation.

X: Frequency of the assoated wave in the WaveBank.
r1=X
r2= X * ".25" - Two Octaves Below X
r3= X * ".50" - One Octaves Below X
r4= X * 2 - One Octaves Above X
r5= X * 4 - Two Octaves Above X

Note: if a wave column is left blank, no wave will be generated. Try changing thse constants to other values to get a different harmonic structure.

Y: Not Used
Z: Volume + Amplitude of WaveBank. If the amplitude is 0, no output is generated
(conserves DSP processing).

WaveShaped:
WaveShaped:  A recursively modulated preset with digital Echo with HPF applied. Two oscillators (one with LFO frequency modulation) wave shape a third oscillator while a fourth oscillator modulates the Spectral Balance of the waveshaped oscillator. The output of the waveshaped oscillator is used to phase modulate the two waveshaping oscillators. The output of the waveshaped oscillator goes into a low pass filter and then to the outputs. This all creates a background motion on the overmodulated echoing result.

Note: One of the few presets using Digital Echo with High Pass Filter recirculation.

Macro i (Filter): Controls the base low pass filter cutoff that is envelope ramped.
Macro ii (EvolDepth): Controls the amount of LFO depth on the Spectral Balance (timbre fluctuation) of the waveshaped oscillator.
Macro iii (ShapeDepth): Controls the amount of waveshaping applied.

X: Pitch
Y: Tone - Controls the low pass filter bandwdth.

Windtube Double Reed:
Windtube Double Reed: Almost identical preset to "'Windtube Air Reed'". A few different multipliers and offsets are used but the main difference is that the BiqGraph graphs are totally different between the two presets. Instead of stressing the even harmonics, here both even and odd mode amplitudes are graphed in a more or less descending order. The 1A offsets (Z controlled) make bit of change but the 2A offsets (Y controlled) drastically reduce higher harmonics.

Note: Compare this preset to "'Windtube Air Reed'" and "'Windtube Single Reed'" and study the BiqGraph graphs of each. This shows how changing the harmonic content of those graphs can drastically affect the sound. Of course you want to feed the BiqGraph a spectra that is rich in harmonics so you can best carve out the sound desired. Try going into the BiqGraph Graph and reducing the Odd amplitudes (dark red lines) in the Mode Amplitudes graph. Reduce each a bit as they descend. A more flute like sound will result. Now go back in and reduce the even amplitudes in descending order. A more clarinet-like timbre will result. Always turn down the gain when experimenting, especially with the Biquad filters. 

Macro i (Body): Controls the convolution body through the full range (0..3) of default responses: Wood->Metal->Fiber->Wood.

Y: Tone. Greatly filters the sound by controlling the Frequency Spread and Bandwidth of the BiqGraph. Lower harmonics decrease as you move to top of Y.

Zazipad:
Zazipad:  A pad is created using a Saw WaveBank, Oscillators and a Signal multiplier along with Swept Echo recirculation. A Sawtooth WaveBank with three waves set an octave apart (with LFO motion on Duty Cycle) is sent to a low Pass filter. A Phase Generator oscillator is used to phase modulate a DSF oscillator which is sent in parallel into a high pass filter and into the low pass filter along with the Phase Generator. Finally the Phase Generator signal is multiplied with itself using a signal multiplier and everything is sent to the outputs.

Note 1: This preset relies on the Signal Multiplier function new to V8.71 and above.

Note 2: Subtle convolution Macro is applied in this preset using a slow triangle LFO modulation on convolution response in a range 0..1. This dynamically change the convolution interpolation in the Metal-to-Metal range with Convolution Lengths ranging 88 to 101. Look at formula M and the Convolution Responses panel. This adds subtle timbral change to the pad effect. A fine range of convolution changes are possible by adjusting the Length parameter within a single convolution response.

Y: Tone - Controls the amount of phase modulation by the Phase Generator oscillator.
Z: Volume + Tone (Controls the low pass filter cutoff frequency)

Zuie:
Zuie: An Oscillator with shape generator (ramped) control of Spectral Balance (once per second) is sent to SL/SR. In parallel a HarMan (set mBiraski) with shape generator control of its interpolation between spectra is sent to a high pass filter and then to SL/SR.

Note: Part of the timbre pulsing in he background of this preset is due to the dynamic triangle motion (once per second) on the Convolution response (in formula "H" on column "Cn1"). This ramps up and down from 0..1. This will then affect motion between the first two convolution responses (set here as Waterphone and Fiber). Try disabling formula H. This will set a constant response on convolution 0 (Waterphone here). You will hear that the dynamic once per second pulsing timbre is reduced as there is no motion back and forth between convolution responses. Try setting "W" in formula "H" to a value of "3.0". This will move the triangle shape through the full range of all four convolution responses. Try setting them to different values to hear a greater timbre shifting through all responses.

ContinuuMini Note: This is a preset where the Mini's limited Y range can be noticed. The repetitions control using Y will be most easily manipulated in the center 2/3 of the fingerboard. If you cannot fully control Y repetitions at the ends of the fingerboard, this is expected operation for the ContinuuMini.

Zwei Baende with Noise:
Zwei Baende with Noise: A variation on Zwei Band with added note component. Two oscillators an octave apart (ever so slightly detuned) are sent in parallel into two band pass filters, each of whose cutoff frequencies and bandwidths are controlled by different Controls and sent to SL/SR outputs. In addition, a sine oscillator is sent independently to the outputs as a third (and fixed) sonic component.

Note: This preset is a study in the use of the band pass filter.

Macro i (Freq1): Cutoff Frequency control of band pass filter #1.
Macro ii (Res1): Bandwidth/resonance control of band pass filter #1.
Macro iii (Freq2): Cutoff Frequency control of band pass filter #2.
Macro iv (Res2): Bandwidth/resonance control of band pass filter #2.
v (Farbe): Color/Convolution. Controls convolution response through the full range of (0..3) mapping to: Wood->Metal->Snap->Fiber. 
vi (Mischung): Mix. Controls the Mix of the bandpass filter output to the fixed sine tone output. As Control vi values increase, the amplitude of the bandpass filters increases and the amplitude of the sine tone decreases.
